;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Afghan peace process]], [[August 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***At least 14 security forces are killed across [[Afghanistan]] in attacks in [[Takhar Province|Takhar]], [[Badakhshan Province|Badakhshan]], and [[Kabul]]. The [[Taliban]] claims responsibility for the first two attacks but denies involvement in Kabul's. The group reiterated that it will not enter peace talks with the [[government of Afghanistan|government]] until all prisoners are released. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/afghanistan-14-security-forces-killed-attacks-200822111402959.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo massacres]]
**Suspected [[Islamist]] militants kill 13 people during raids on two villages in eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], the [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|army]] and a village chief report. It is the latest of such attacks that the [[United Nations]] says may be [[war crime]]s. The [[Allied Democratic Forces]] (ADF) have killed more than 1,000 people since 2019, according to UN figures. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-violence/suspected-islamist-militants-kill-13-in-eastern-congo-villages-idUSKBN25I0D1 (Reuters)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Three [[massacre]]s kill 28 people, in [[Arauca Department|Arauca]], [[Cauca Department|Cauca]], and [[Nariño]]. These complete a week with five massacres, adding up to more than 33 this year. Gangs are believed to be responsible for nearly 80 percent of massacres in Colombia this year, the vast majority of them occurring in [[departments of Colombia|departments]] with illegal [[coca production in Colombia|coca-producing]] enclaves. [https://colombiareports.com/colombia-ends-terrifying-week-with-three-massacres-in-one-day/ (Colombia Reports)] [https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/latin-america/united-nations-condemns-spike-in-colombia-massacres.phtml (''Buenos Aires Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**Two simultaneous tropical storms, Laura and Marco, threaten [[Gulf Coast]] residents in the coming days. Laura is currently over [[Puerto Rico]], while Marco is making its way through the [[Yucatan Channel]]. This would mark the first time in over 60 years in which two tropical storms were active simultaneously in the [[Gulf of Mexico]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/22/weather/tropical-storm-laura-marco-atlantic-gulf-forecast-saturday/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/21/weather/atlantic-tropical-development-forecast-friday/index.html (CNN<sup>2</sup>)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
**At least 13 people are killed after [[National Police of Peru|police]] raid a nightclub in [[Lima]] for breaching restrictions that were imposed in response to the pandemic. Police report that a stampede occurred as patrons tried to escape, resulting in casualties, while others were killed due to [[asphyxiation]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/at-least-13-crushed-to-death-as-peru-police-raid-clandestine-club-party/story-uaK8UsOuw1TbJqeSUQbjaJ.html (Reuters via ''Hindustan Times'')]
*A [[cargo aircraft]] [[2020 Juba AN-26 crash|crashes]] upon [[takeoff]] from [[Juba International Airport]] in [[Juba]], [[South Sudan]], en route to the cities of [[Aweil]] and [[Wau, South Sudan|Wau]], killing at least 17 people. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-08/22/c_139310179.htm (Xinhua)]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] announces a ban of large gatherings, shutting down high-risk facilities, banning in-person churches, and removing fans from professional sports nationwide tomorrow, as the country reports a new five-month high of 332 new cases in the last 24 hours, citing "a very dangerous situation that could trigger a massive nationwide spread of COVID-19". [https://news.detik.com/internasional/d-5142523/kasus-terus-melonjak-korsel-bersiap-hadapi-gelombang-kedua-corona (AFP via detikNews)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/08/22/south-korea-announces-unprecedented-restrictions-curb-spread/ (''The Telegraph'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****India reports a record jump in infections, recording 69,878 new cases and nearing three million. It also reported 945 new deaths, bringing the tally to 55,794. 62,282 patients recovered from the disease, which is also the highest in a single day. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-digest-india-registers-record-jump-as-cases-near-3-million/a-54658318 (DW)]
****India reaches milestone of 10 lakh (1 million) tests per day. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/govt-reaches-target-of-testing-a-million-people-in-a-day/story-6G33zy5k3VTi5ZF2u7r4bP.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] signs a deal with [[China|Chinese]] company [[Sinovac Biotech]] to purchase 50 million doses of a [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-08-22/indonesia-signs-agreement-with-sinovac-for-covid-19-vaccine (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Robert Koch Institute]] reports more than 2,000 new cases in Germany in the last 24 hours, which is the highest number of reported cases since late April. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/08/22/covid-19-germany-reports-highest-number-of-new-cases-since-the-end-of-april (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The number of daily new cases in [[Italy]] surpasses 1,000 for the first time since May. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/italy-sees-over-1000-daily-covid-19-cases-for-1st-time-since-mid-may (''Daily Sabah'')]

;International relations
*A 90-minute meeting held between delegates representing the [[Economic Community of West African States]] and leaders of the [[2020 Malian coup d'état|recent coup d'état in Mali]] over a return to civilian rule is cut short to 20 minutes for unknown reasons. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/malis-coup-leaders-meet-mediators-seeking-return-to-civilian-rule-idUSKBN25I0FI?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd Protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon]] 
***[[Department of Homeland Security]] officers force demonstrators out of a plaza near [[Multnomah County Justice Center]] as dueling demonstrations in [[Portland, Oregon]] by [[Proud Boys|right-wing]] and [[Antifa (United States) |left-wing protesters]] turn violent. Images show hundreds of people involved, many of them wearing helmets and carrying makeshift shields. Some demonstrators appeared to use [[pepper spray]] and at least one person appeared to pull a gun, but no arrests have been made so far. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/portland-protest-turns-violent-federal-police-clear-plaza-n1237784 (NBC News)]
**[[George Floyd protests in Michigan]]
***Forty people are arrested while protesting [[Operation Legend]] in [[Detroit]]. Police also used [[tear gas]] and pepper spray on the crowd of about 100 people. [https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2020/08/23/dozens-of-protesters-on-woodward-avenue-tear-gassed-arrested-downtown/ (WDIV)]
*Sudanese [[Prime minister of Sudan|prime minister]] [[Abdalla Hamdok]] says that Sudan is ready to cooperate with the [[International Criminal Court]] (ICC) to facilitate the international body access to alleged war criminals over the [[Darfur War]], including former ruler [[Omar al-Bashir]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-politics/sudan-ready-to-cooperate-with-icc-over-darfur-says-pm-idUSKBN25I0P3?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[2020 United States Postal Service crisis]]
***In a 257–150 vote, the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] approves a bill that would reverse changes to the operations of the [[United States Postal Service|Postal Service]] implemented by [[United States Postmaster General|Postmaster General]] [[Louis DeJoy]], amid a series of backlogs and delays in the delivery of mail following his appointment in June. The bill also aims to provide the agency financial support worth [[United States dollar|$]]25 billion in preparation for an expected surge in [[postal voting]] in the [[2020 United States presidential election|upcoming election]] due to the pandemic. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1325827/us-house-passes-bill-to-reverse-changes-blamed-for-mail-delays (AP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[2020 Ivorian presidential election]]
**Incumbent [[President of the Ivory Coast|President]] [[Alassane Ouattara]] is formally chosen by his party, the [[Rally of the Republicans]], to run for a third term in the October election. However, opposition and civil society groups claim the move is unconstitutional, as the [[Constitution of Ivory Coast|Constitution]] limits a president to only two terms. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200822-ivory-coast-rejects-election-bids-of-ex-president-gbagbo-ex-rebel-leader-soro (France 24)]
*[[2020 Northern Territory general election]]
**[[Australia]]'s [[Northern Territory]] re-elects the incumbent [[Australian Labor Party (Northern Territory Branch)|Labor Party]] government. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-08-24/nt-labor-and-michael-gunner-to-form-majority-government/12586980 (ABC)]
*[[Alexei Navalny]] is admitted to the [[Charité]] hospital in [[Berlin]], Germany, following a medical evacuation flight from [[Omsk]], Russia. The chairman of the [[Cinema for Peace Foundation]], which organized the evacuation, says the [[coma]]tose [[Russian opposition]] leader is in a "stable condition". [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/21/europe/alexey-navalny-germany-flight-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
